text: Every time you try to criticize the police, people get the exact same response. It's a dangerous job. If you don't like it, you do it. Okay, bet. I'm going to start naming jobs I've done that have more fatalities than being a police officer. Number one, being a public school student. It's not funny, is it? There were over 300 school shootings in 2022 alone with over 330 victims. The entire police force across the country, there were less than 50 firearm deaths last year. You guys may remember that a couple of months ago, I debunked the myth that being the pregnant wife of a police officer is more dangerous than actually being a police officer. For some reason, the fact that being a police officer is a dangerous job just doesn't sit right with some people. So here we have another guy who decided to compare jobs he has done with the dangers of being a cop. And the first thing he mentions is being a public school student. First of all, being a student is not a job, so you are already off here. But okay, let's roll with this example. And by the way, if you were a student, it seems like you are not the best one, because otherwise you would know that when you compare two statistics with completely different population sizes, you need to control for population and use a per person measure, or as they say in Latin, per capita. You cannot simply compare two absolute numbers. There were approximately 49.6 million public school students in 2022. Meanwhile, there were an estimated 860,000 sworn law enforcement officers nationwide. And before anyone asks why I'm using 2022 data, because that is the year his own school data comes from, I am checking his comparison, not making a new one. So even if we take your numbers, 332 school shooting victims compared with 49 police officers killed with firearms, we get approximately 0.67 victims per 100,000 students compared with 5.7 death per 100,000 police officers. So even using your completely broken comparison, the figure for police officers is still around eight and a half times higher. Why is your comparison completely broken? Because the numbers you are comparing are not apples to apples. For schools, you use victims, which includes people who were injured but survived. For police officers, you use only those who were killed with firearms. Two different things. Your 332 figure comes from a broad school shooting database and includes people who were either injured or killed. An Iowa Education Week tracker counted 140 people injured or killed in school shootings in 2022. Of those, 40 were killed, 32 students or other children, and 8 adults. Meanwhile, 49 police officers were intentionally killed with firearms that year. So if we compare firearm death with firearm death, we get approximately 0.065 death per 100,000 students compared with 5.7 per 100,000 police officers. That makes the rate among police officers roughly 88 times higher. So yes, you can criticize the police, but you should also have some respect for the people doing a genuinely dangerous job, and stop misrepresenting the risks they face just because the truth doesn't fit your argument.
